title: The Old Year Now Hath Passed Away
description: The Old Year Now Hath Passed Away in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Steuerlein wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 173.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The old year now hath passed a-way, We thank Thee, Christ, our Lord, to day That Thou hast kept us through the year When dan-ger and dis-tress were near.

lines: The old year now hath passed away,
We thank Thee, Christ, our Lord, to-day
That Thou hast kept us through the year
When danger and distress were near.
We pray Thee, O eternal Son,
Who with the Father reign’st as one,
To guard and rule Thy Christendom
Through all the ages yet to come.
Take not Thy saving Word away,
Our souls’ true comfort, staff, and stay;
Abide with us and keep us free
From all false doctrines graciously.
O help us to forsake all sin,
A new and holier course begin;
From last year’s sins, Lord, hide Thy face,
In this new year grant us Thy grace,
That as true Christians we may live
Or die in peace that Thou wilt give,
To rise again when Thou shalt come,
And enter our eternal home.

licence: Public domain: Johann Steuerlein died in 1613; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Johann Steuerlein (1546–1613), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
